title: RAII and ownership in C++
summary: Replace manual new and delete with a smart pointer, then review a lifetime bug.

scenario.briefing: A device driver allocates a reading and sometimes forgets to release it. Replace the manual allocation with an owning smart pointer.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Diagnose a realistic mistake and choose the correct repair.

hints: The return type already promises exclusive ownership.
std::make_unique allocates and constructs in one step.
Remove the raw new and the empty unique_ptr.

misconceptions.description: Using new and returning an empty unique_ptr.
misconceptions.testDescription: Allocation is owned by make_unique, not a raw new.
misconceptions.feedback: The raw allocation leaks because no owner receives it. Return make_unique<int>(value).
Unique ownership cannot be copied. Move it or return it by value.

misconceptions.description: Returning a reference to a local object.
misconceptions.feedback: Making the string static changes one lifetime bug into shared mutable state. Return by value.

misconceptions.description: Believing every make_unique needs a matching delete.
misconceptions.feedback: RAII releases the allocation automatically when the unique_ptr goes out of scope.

sections.title: C++ functions and collections
sections.body: Functions declare return and parameter types: int add(int left, int right) { return left + right; }. std::vector<int> values = { 3, -1, 2 }; owns a growable array and reports its size. Templates such as std::vector<T> are checked when instantiated.

sections.title: C++ errors and tools
sections.body: Exceptions signal failures that callers can catch. std::optional models a value that may be absent. g++ or clang++ compiles, CMake configures builds, and sanitizers expose lifetime and bounds errors.

steps.title: The dangling reference
steps.prompt: This function returns a reference to a local string. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.

fixes.label: Return std::string by value instead of by reference.
Make the local string static and keep the reference.
Return a pointer to the local string.

steps.explanation: A reference to a local object dangles after the function returns. Returning by value gives the caller an owned string.
hints: A reference to a local object is invalid after return.
The local string is destroyed when the function exits.
Return ownership or copy the value instead.
Change the return type to std::string and return by value.

steps.title: RAII and ownership

statements.label: A unique_ptr releases its object when the pointer goes out of scope.
A unique_ptr can be copied like a raw pointer.
std::make_unique transfers ownership to the returned unique_ptr.
Every make_unique must be paired with an explicit delete.

steps.explanation: RAII makes release automatic. unique_ptr expresses exclusive ownership and cannot be copied.
